learning_objective: The learner will critique eight draft survey questions as good or problematic and name the problem in each problematic question, with at least 7 of 8 verdicts correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** survey-question-reviewer
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** critique
**Learning Objective:** The learner will critique eight draft survey questions as good or problematic and name the problem in each problematic question, with at least 7 of 8 verdicts correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Student Survey (defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each question the learner commits Good or Problem, and for a Problem picks its kind from Leading, Double-barreled, or Vague. A verdict is correct when it matches the Correct verdict column in Content, and the kind is checked in the feedback. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 verdicts correct on the first attempt. Reading the five rules is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A longer question gets a better answer. (2) A positive question is a neutral question. (3) Asking two things at once saves time. **Instructional Rationale:** Critiquing a question against the survey rules is an Evaluate-level action. Questions that fail in different ways, and four sound ones, teach the learner to read each question as a student would. **Content:** The two verdicts: Good, Problem. The kinds of problem: Leading, Double-barreled, Vague. The eight draft questions (all made up): | # | Draft question | Correct verdict | Kind of problem | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | The lesson helped me understand what a watershed is. (1 to 5, disagree to agree) | Good | None | It is neutral, specific, and about one idea. | | 2 | Did you enjoy the great new simulation? | Problem | Leading | The word "great" pushes students toward yes. | | 3 | The lesson was clear and the quiz was fair. | Problem | Double-barreled | It asks two things at once. | | 4 | The lesson was good. | Problem | Vague | It does not say what to fix. | | 5 | I could read or hear every part of the lesson without help. (1 to 5, disagree to agree) | Good | None | It is neutral and specific, and it asks about access. | | 6 | Which parts of the lesson, if any, were hard to use? (open answer) | Good | None | It is neutral and invites specific answers. | | 7 | Don't you agree that the explanations were helpful? | Problem | Leading | It asks the student to agree. | | 8 | I would like more lessons like this one. (1 to 5, disagree to agree) | Good | None | It is neutral and about one idea. | **Provenance:** The questions are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The rules follow the chapter section "Student Survey". **Rules:** Each question has exactly one correct verdict, four per verdict. The four problems are two Leading, one Double-barreled, and one Vague. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one draft question. 2. The learner chooses Good or Problem. For a Problem the learner also picks its kind. 3. The sim shows whether the verdict was correct, the kind of problem, and the Why text. 4. After question 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 questions in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [verdict]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This question is [verdict]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can write fair survey questions." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed question. **Starting State:** The first question in the shuffled order and the two verdicts. The question shown is "Would this question get an honest answer?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists five rules for survey questions, and its examples of a leading question, a double-barreled question, and a vague question appear in the sim.
